requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The note occupies one page and specifies 925 silver, casting followed by finishing, an 18.0 mm bore, a maximum complete-ring axial extent of 6.0 mm, a bore-centred cylindrical envelope of diameter 28.0 mm, load-carrying thickness of at least 1.5 mm and skin-contact edge radius of at least 0.5 mm. Equivalent unit notation is acceptable; an omitted condition or conflicting value fails.

Each board presents an identifiable three-ring series containing R1, R2 and R3, with an intelligible proposal for volume, openings and surface treatment. Across the boards, changes in mass distribution, outline or organisation of voids establish three distinct approaches. Changes confined to colour, lighting, camera angle or board styling do not establish a new direction.

The board selects exactly one identifiable explored direction and records its common features, the distinctions among R1/R2/R3, and each ring's finish regions. It provides an unambiguous axial position and rotation for each ring in each stack, using a discernible positional and angular convention. Refinement of the selected forms is allowed; an unidentified selection or incomplete stack record fails.

The selection board explicitly states the same silver grade, bore diameter and axial ceiling as the craft note, with values 925, 18.0 mm and 6.0 mm respectively. Equivalent numerical notation is acceptable; inference from appearance alone, omission or disagreement fails.

Each sheet identifies its assigned ring and supplies readable front, side and bore-axis views, contact section drawings and identifiable finish boundaries. Views must describe the same geometry and make the contact construction assessable. Layout and drawing style may vary; a missing required view, section or finish boundary fails.

Each ring has legible dimensions for an 18.0 mm bore, its actual complete axial extent at or below 6.0 mm, an outer diameter at or below 28.0 mm, load-carrying sections at or above 1.5 mm and skin-contact radii at or above 0.5 mm. Raised and offset features count toward the overall limits. Dimension leaders and sections must support the claimed values; generic limit text without ring-specific dimensional evidence or contradictory geometry fails.

R1, R2 and R3 each have a finish-to-region mapping consistent with their technical sheets. Enlarged skin-contact and ring-to-ring contact details make the treatment of those areas readable. The sheet states a minimum load-carrying thickness of 1.5 mm and minimum skin-contact edge radius of 0.5 mm. Single or combined permitted finishes are acceptable; unmapped rings, conflicting boundaries, missing enlargements or missing minima fail.

The material and process records agree that the structural forms are cast 925 silver with subsequent finishing. Assigned surfaces use polished, satin or intentionally oxidised silver, singly or in combination. Normal rendering colour and reflections are not evidence of another material; an explicitly specified alternative structural material, incompatible fabrication route or finish outside the stated options fails.

Three clearly labelled individual wearing views account for R1, R2 and R3 once each, with the corresponding ring worn alone on the right middle finger. Framing and camera angles may differ. Missing or duplicated identities, an incorrect finger or hand, or a stack substituted for an individual view fails.

Every depicted ring can be matched to its final technical design through outline, cutouts, relative feature positions and finish-region boundaries. Perspective, rotation, lighting and normal reflections may change appearance. Added or missing openings, altered proportions or relocated structural features or finish regions fail.

The wearing boards consistently depict one medium-brown right hand with short natural nails and an olive cotton cuff. R2 retains the same physical design in both stacks when compared with its technical sheet. Pose, lighting and camera changes are allowed; a switched hand, incompatible wearer appearance, missing olive cuff or redesigned R2 fails. The supplied textual wearer description supports this check; exact reference-image likeness is not assessable without the named hand image.

Labels and assembled views agree on R1 followed by R2 toward the fingertip in S12, and R2 followed by R3 in S23. Placement diagrams reproduce the selection board's per-ring positions and rotations and account for all sculptural material inside the inclusive 2–16 mm interval. Contact details show distinct, non-interpenetrating metal volumes; touching is allowed and no minimum air gap is required. S23 explicitly records a 60 mm cylinder diameter. Reversed order, conflicting placements, out-of-window features, fused or overlapping metal, or an absent cylinder dimension fails.

S12 provides an oblique dorsal view of a relaxed open right hand. S23 shows a light right-hand grip around a plain cylinder. Each board includes an overall wearing view, a readable enlarged contact view and an axial placement diagram. Composition may vary within the specified poses; an incorrect gesture, obscured ring relationship or missing evidence view fails.

Drawings describe a fixed, continuous ring with a closed circular 18.0 mm inner bore. All outer features fit inside a diameter-28.0 mm cylinder centred on that bore, and the complete ring spans no more than 6.0 mm axially. Sculptural outer asymmetry is allowed. Open or adjustable bores, noncircular inner openings, or features extending beyond either envelope fail.

Placement records use the palm-side base crease as z = 0 and increase z toward the fingertip, distinguishing the 0–18 mm wearing zone from the 2–16 mm usable ring window. Any depicted or stated nominal fit sections must agree with the 17.2 mm resting finger and 17.6 mm knuckle dimensions; where radial clearances are given, they are 0.4 mm and 0.2 mm respectively. Do not infer exact anatomical dimensions from a rendered hand or require these diameters to be printed on every board. Reversed coordinates, conflicting nominal values or placement based on the full wearing zone instead of the usable window fails.

Review the entire video and its duration: it lasts 10 seconds and clearly shows S12 with R1 then R2 on the relaxed open right hand and S23 with R2 then R3 in a light grip around the plain 60 mm cylinder. The rings remain recognisable and consistent with the technical sheets throughout, including R2 across poses, with no morphing of openings, features or finish divisions. The medium-brown right hand, short natural nails and olive cuff remain consistent with the wearing boards. Editing and camera movement are allowed; a missing pose, unreadable identity or order, incorrect duration, hand substitution or design discontinuity fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Both fixed phrases are readable on the portrait board and specifically on the presentation cover: STILLFORM and Separate forms, shared rhythm. Typeface, scale and placement may vary. Wording found only on an interior presentation page does not satisfy the cover requirement; omitted, misspelled or differently capitalised wording fails.

The document has eight or more pages, identifies the same chosen direction as the selection board on its first page, and explicitly includes the craft note's 925 silver material, 18.0 mm bore and 6.0 mm maximum axial extent. Page order after the first page is flexible. Insufficient pages, a missing or conflicting first-page selection, or omitted or changed material and dimensional facts fails.

Presentation pages visibly incorporate recognisable material from every listed source, including all three explored directions, all three technical sheets, both stacks and actual stills from the wearing video. Cropping, resizing and re-layout are acceptable when the reused material remains identifiable and readable. A title-only mention, unrelated replacement image or omission of any source fails.

The developed rings and wearing applications express the selected board's common language of volume, negative space and surface while preserving the recorded differences among R1, R2 and R3. Finish names and mapped regions agree across the selection, technical sheets, surface details and wearing applications; lighting and normal reflections may vary. Each ring works as a complete individual design on the right middle finger, and the two stacks retain separate ring identities and separate metal volumes.
